To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the p1 gene directs the biosynthesis of maysin in maize silks and 2) the tissue specificity of p1 transgenes is variable and can be controlled epigenetically.

transformation of maize with the P1 transcription factor directs the production of silk mason, a corn ear worm resistance factor, in a manner that is concordant with a hierarchy of tissue-specific expression.

the p1 transgene directs maysin accumulation to maize silk tissue and that the pigmentation pattern of p1 transgenic maize plants is controlled by a hierarchy of tissue-specific expression that may be due to epigenetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the p1 gene to confer resistance to corn ear worm in maize.
the production of maize plants with improved resistance to insect pests.
the production of plants that have increased resistance to insect pests and that have improved traits for other uses, such as food or feed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p1 promoter is not a tissue specific promoter.
p1 expression is necessary, but not sufficient, for maysin accumulation.
the p1 promoter is a good promoter for the production of transgenics with improved silk maysin content, but that the promoter is not a reliable tool for the production of tissue-specific transgenes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p1 promoter is not a tissue-specific promoter and that the p1 transgene can induce the production of maysin and pigments in maize tissues other than silk.
the p1 transgene directs maysin production to the silk tissues in a manner that is consistent with a hierarchy of organ-specific pigmentation.

the p1 promoter can direct maysin production in silk tissues and can confer pigmentation to multiple tissues of the maize plants, but that the tissue specificity of the transgene can vary amongst transgenic plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tissue specificity of a transgenic promoter can vary in unpredictable ways amongst transgenic lines, and that the observed variation can have important consequences for the expression of introduced traits.
tissue specificity of transgene expression is not a binary trait, but rather a spectrum of expression that is influenced by factors that can be difficult to predict.
the tissue-specific expression of a transgene can vary in unexpected ways in the transgenic plant.
